description: A Windows memory image's OS and capture time, live/scanned process views and tree, command lines, handles, services, network connections, suspicious executable regions, VADs, kernel modules and loaded DLLs (Volatility 3, the image's symbols first). When the image holds no symbol table for the kernel, it names the kernel (PDB, GUID, age) as missing, which stops a kickoff unless --allow-missing-symbols.
exclusions: every Volatility plugin other than windows.info and the eleven listed (no registry, file, timeline or YARA scan)
Linux and macOS memory images, and hibernation or crash-dump variants Volatility does not open
an image whose kernel symbols are neither in the image nor fetched from the symbol server (the network may not allow it)
memory the capture did not hold: paged-out or swapped regions
covers: What windows.info and the eleven listed Volatility plugins report with symbols already in the image. Linux and macOS images, unsupported hibernation/crash-dump variants, YARA rules and every other plugin are not covered; symbols come from the image first, and from the symbol server only when the image has none for the kernel and the job's network allows it, which coverage says.
